title: Hierarchical adaptive router with confidence-delta prefill probes and graceful fallback
creator: Sofia Mendes
description: Prototype a hierarchical, adaptive routing layer for speculative decoding that uses low-cost prefill probes and a confidence-delta acceptance metric to decide when to accept optimistic decode outputs versus falling back to a conservative decode path. The goal is to increase throughput and reduce average latency for short-turn requests without degrading quality or SLOs. This ticket captures design decisions, measurement plan, rollout strategy, and fallback behavior for runtime implementation and experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Router prototype integrated with runtime traffic gate and feature-flagged for canary rollout
Confidence-delta metric implemented in runtime and exposed to tracing and metrics APIs
Fallback path that performs conservative decode with KV-warmup works end-to-end and preserves token ordering and session state
End-to-end A/B experiment shows >=15% p50 token-latency reduction on targeted workloads with quality regression <= 0.5% on eval prompt set
No increase in 99th-percentile error rate or user-visible hallucination incidents during canary
design_decisions: Two-tier router: Level 1 lightweight probe using a truncated prefill (stride-based probe up to 8 tokens) evaluated on a lightweight kernel; Level 2 full decode only if probe fails acceptance
Acceptance metric is confidence-delta: softmax logit gap between top-1 and top-2 normalized by token position and kernel signature to account for quantization noise
Kernel-satisfiability score included: a cheap static fingerprint check to prefer kernels with lower expected numerical variance for acceptance decisions
State reconciliation: optimistic KVs are kept ephemeral; if fallback triggers, conservative decode reconstructs KVs deterministically from original prefill and replay of probe tokens
Feature-flagged rollout with thresholds configurable per-customer, model, and route
Observability: emit per-request probe_score, confidence_delta, kernel_fingerprint, and fallback_reason for offline analysis
rollout_plan: Step 0: Unit and integration tests + deterministic replay harness to validate deterministic fallback behavior
Step 1: Internal Canary with synthetic traffic (100k requests) on a staging cluster to validate metrics pipeline
Step 2: External Canary on <5% of production read-only traffic for low-risk customers with explicit opt-in
Step 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with automated rollback triggers for quality regressions and error spikes
Step 4: Full rollout gated on meeting latency and quality SLAs for 72h during ramp
experiment_plan: A/B buckets: control (no speculative route) vs probe-enabled router
Primary metrics: p50 token latency, p95 request latency, decode tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens
Quality guardrails: automated eval against a curated prompt set and semantic similarity checks with thresholded acceptance
Exploratory telemetry: distribution of confidence-delta by model, kernel, and sequence length
Heatmap analysis: probe length vs acceptance rate and delta in latency/quality tradeoffs
metrics_and_alerts: probe_accept_rate: percentage of probes accepted by confidence-delta
probe_reject_rate: percentage falling back to conservative decode
p50_token_latency_by_route: goal decrease >=15% for targeted use-cases
quality_regression_rate: percent of eval prompts with lower semantic score than baseline (alert if >0.5%)
fallback_volume: absolute number of fallbacks (alert if spike >3x baseline within 15m)
kernel_mismatch_alert: if kernel_fingerprint correlates with lowered acceptance across >10% of traffic
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probe may introduce additional variance causing nondeterministic behavior. Mitigation: enforce deterministic pseudo-random seeds and replay harness for each session
Risk: Acceptance metric may bias toward shorter prefixes causing silent quality regressions. Mitigation: require semantic-similarity evaluation and maintain per-route quality budgets
Risk: Increased complexity in KV lifecycle causing memory leaks. Mitigation: ephemeral KVs with strict lifecycle tied to request and GC checks in integration tests
Risk: Kernel-dependent numeric drift could make acceptance decisions noisy. Mitigation: kernel_satisfiability score and per-kernel thresholds configured via telemetry
Risk: Unexpected cost increase from probes. Mitigation: cost cap per-session and dynamic probe frequency throttling
